note: Source-language strings for protocol 0.1.0. Plain-language drafts, not medically reviewed. Hindi and Marathi translations are added in M2 and stay needs_review until a native-speaking doctor approves them.

strings.common.return_immediately_fallback: If the person gets worse in any way, go to a hospital now.
strings.dengue.action.ask_blood_test: Ask for a blood test: complete blood count with platelets and haematocrit.
strings.dengue.action.call_help: Call 108 or 112, or go to the nearest hospital emergency department now.
strings.dengue.action.check_painkillers: Before taking painkillers such as ibuprofen, diclofenac, aspirin or mefenamic acid, check with a doctor or pharmacist. They may not be safe when dengue is possible.
strings.dengue.action.dont_wait: Do not wait to see if it gets better.
strings.dengue.action.get_tested: Get tested, as described under testing advice.
strings.dengue.action.go_if_worse: If any warning sign appears, go to a hospital at once.
strings.dengue.action.keep_fluids: Keep drinking fluids such as ORS, fruit juice, milk, or barley or rice water. Plain water alone is not enough. If there is diabetes, ask the doctor which fluids are right.
strings.dengue.action.recheck_if_fever: If fever starts or any symptom appears, answer these questions again.
strings.dengue.action.review_daily: Have a doctor review the person every day until the risky days are over.
strings.dengue.action.see_doctor_today: See a doctor today, in person.
strings.dengue.action.tell_doctor: Tell the doctor when the fever started, which medicines were taken, and any blood test results.
strings.dengue.headline.emergency: Get to a hospital now. Call 108 or 112.
strings.dengue.headline.home_care: No danger signs reported right now. Keep watching: this can change quickly.
strings.dengue.headline.test_monitor: Get tested and keep watching closely.
strings.dengue.note.critical_phase: Days 3 to 7 of illness are the critical phase. Danger can start when the fever settles. Watch closely for 1 to 2 days after the fever falls.
strings.dengue.note.fever_gone: The fever going away is not good news by itself in these days. Keep checking for warning signs.
strings.dengue.reason.blood_or_black_stool: Black stool, or blood in the stool.
strings.dengue.reason.child_fewer_wet_diapers: A young child with fever who is passing less urine than usual.
strings.dengue.reason.child_poor_feeding: A young child with fever who is feeding or drinking poorly.
strings.dengue.reason.critical_phase: Days 3 to 7 of illness are the riskiest, even if the fever goes down.
strings.dengue.reason.danger_sign_without_fever: A warning sign is present even though there is no fever.
strings.dengue.reason.dengue_like_symptoms: Fever with symptoms that can go with dengue.
strings.dengue.reason.drowsy_or_lethargic: Very sleepy, or unusually weak and slow.
strings.dengue.reason.fainting: Fainted, or feels about to faint.
strings.dengue.reason.fever_3d_with_risk: Fever for 3 days or more, with an age, health or living-situation risk.
strings.dengue.reason.fever_over_24h: The fever has lasted more than a day.
strings.dengue.reason.heavy_menstrual_bleeding: Very heavy or unusual bleeding from the vagina.
strings.dengue.reason.hematocrit_up_platelets_do: Haematocrit is going up while platelets are going down.
strings.dengue.reason.infant_fever: Fever in a baby under 12 months.
strings.dengue.reason.input_issues: Some answers look incomplete or do not match each other, so we are being careful.
strings.dengue.reason.lab_marker_positive: A dengue test in the report is positive.
strings.dengue.reason.liver_tests_very_high: Liver blood tests (AST or ALT) in the report are very high.
strings.dengue.reason.no_danger_signs: No danger signs reported right now; this can change quickly.
strings.dengue.reason.no_urine_6h: Little or no urine in the last 6 hours (for a baby: no wet diaper).
strings.dengue.reason.nsaid_with_stomach_pain: Stomach pain after taking a painkiller such as aspirin or ibuprofen.
strings.dengue.reason.platelets_falling_fast: The platelet count is falling fast.
strings.dengue.reason.platelets_low: The platelet count in the report is low.
strings.dengue.reason.platelets_very_low: The platelet count in the report is very low.
strings.dengue.reason.rash_pain_outbreak: Fever with a rash and bad headache, eye pain or body pain during the dengue season.
strings.dengue.reason.reduced_fetal_movement: The baby in the womb is moving less than usual.
strings.dengue.reason.risk_floor: Fever that is lasting, together with a risk factor: see a doctor today.
strings.dengue.reason.risk_step_up: Because of age, a health condition or living situation, the urgency was raised by one step.
strings.dengue.reason.severe_abdominal_pain: Strong belly pain, or belly pain that is getting worse.
strings.dengue.reason.uncertain_danger: Not sure about a warning sign, so we advise seeing a doctor today.
strings.dengue.reason.unknown_emergency: Not sure about a serious sign, so it is treated as urgent.
strings.dengue.reason.warning_as_fever_falls: A warning sign has appeared as the fever went down. This is when dengue can turn serious.
strings.dengue.return.baby_crying: A young baby who cries a lot and cannot be comforted.
strings.dengue.return.bleeding: Any bleeding: red spots on the skin, nose or gum bleeding, blood in vomit, black stool, very heavy periods.
strings.dengue.return.cannot_drink: Cannot drink, or refuses to drink.
strings.dengue.return.cold_pale_clammy: Pale, cold or clammy skin, hands or feet.
strings.dengue.return.severe_headache: A severe headache that does not go away.
strings.dengue.return.sleepy_confused_fit: Unusual sleepiness, confusion, restlessness, or a fit.
strings.dengue.return.worse_as_fever_falls: Feeling worse as the fever goes down.
strings.dengue.risk.lives_alone_or_far: Lives alone, or far from a hospital
strings.dengue.test.cbc: Ask for a complete blood count, with platelets and haematocrit.
strings.dengue.test.igm_later: After day 5 of fever, the IgM antibody test is usually used.
strings.dengue.test.no_rapid_kits: Ask for a laboratory test. The national programme does not recommend rapid test kits.
strings.dengue.test.ns1_early: In the first 5 days of fever, the NS1 antigen test is usually used.
strings.dengue.test.tell_lab: Tell the lab the date the fever started and the date of the test.
strings.dengue.test.timing_unknown: Tell the doctor or lab the date the fever started: the right test depends on the day.
strings.dengue.watch.daily_notes: Note the temperature, drinks and urine every day.
strings.dengue.watch.drinks_and_urine: Check that the person is drinking well and passing urine regularly.
strings.dengue.watch.fever_falls: The riskiest days are usually day 3 to 7. When the fever goes down, stay alert: a falling fever is not a sign of being safe.
strings.dengue.watch.new_symptoms: Look out for new belly pain, vomiting, bleeding, or unusual sleepiness.
